code:
FROM python:3.12-slim

# Start FROM a base image: Python preinstalled on slim Debian.

WORKDIR /app

# All later commands run here; created automatically.

COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

# Copy ONLY the dependency list first, then install. Docker caches layers:

# as long as requirements.txt is unchanged, rebuilds skip the slow install.

COPY . .

# Now copy the application code (changes often, so it goes LAST).

EXPOSE 8000

# Documentation of the listening port (publishing still needs -p at run time).

CMD ["python", "server.py"]

# The default command a container runs at start.
description: A complete Dockerfile for a small Python agent service, ordered so stable layers come first and volatile layers last.

steps.description: Start from the `python:3.12-slim` base image. The comment says this is Python preinstalled on slim Debian, and the page calls a Dockerfile the recipe that builds an image.
Set `WORKDIR /app`. The comment says all later commands run here, and Docker creates the directory automatically.
Copy only `requirements.txt` and install it with `pip install --no-cache-dir -r`. The comments explain the cache rule: as long as `requirements.txt` is unchanged, rebuilds skip the slow install.
Copy the application code last with `COPY . .`. The comment says the code changes often, so it goes last, which keeps the expensive install layer cached.
`EXPOSE 8000` documents the listening port. The comment notes that publishing still needs `-p` at run time, so EXPOSE is documentation, not a publish.

The `CMD` instruction sets the default command a container runs at start, here `python server.py`. The page says the ordering rule, stable layers first and volatile layers last, is the most useful Dockerfile habit.
